title: The Elevator That Stopped on a Floor That Didn't Exist
disclosure: This is an original fictional suspense story. Every visual and music item in this file is a PREVIEW_ONLY approval candidate and is not cleared for release.

story.person: Elias, a night-shift hospital security guard
story.central_question: What opened beyond the elevator doors—and why was Elias already waiting there?
story.risk: If Elias enters the impossible corridor, he may lose the only ordinary reality he can return to.
story.irreversible_decision: Elias steps beyond the elevator threshold after the red emergency lamp appears.
story.consequence: The feed cuts out, then a second passenger is logged while Elias remains in the lobby.
story.wound: Elias has spent years trusting systems that keep people safe, so the system's contradiction attacks his identity.
story.flaw: His professional curiosity overrides the final safe exit.
story.something_to_lose: Elias's safety, identity and claim to know where he is.
story.hook: At 2:14 a.m., a hospital elevator stops at Floor 13 even though the building has only twelve floors.
story.reveal: The second passenger exists in the log while Elias is visibly still outside, changing the anomaly from a broken elevator into a duplicate presence.

beats.text: At 2:14 a.m., a hospital elevator stopped at a floor the building did not have.
The guard on duty checked the panel. There was no button for thirteen. The system log still showed the doors open for forty-seven seconds.
Then the camera found a corridor beyond the doors: narrow concrete, one red emergency lamp, and no sign of construction. Elias stepped forward. The feed went black.
By morning, maintenance had found no thirteenth landing. The control board was replaced. The elevator was chained shut.
At 2:14 the next night, the display returned to thirteen.
This time, the camera stayed on. A figure in Elias's uniform stood at the far end of the red corridor.
The lobby monitor showed Elias outside the elevator, watching. Then the system added a second passenger.
The indicator began descending below the basement. No one pressed a button.
